text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Dedicated pool node preempt/evict detected in pool 'vault-prod-ded-2' (region: us-west2). Tenant: Cerulean Health. Symptoms: sudden 503s and increased latency for rdl-13b-v1; provider preempt signal + kernel oops on GPU. Paging oncall.

oncall-jordan: Acked. I'm on it — pulling logs and opening runbook. tagging eng-runtime and infra.

ops-kyra: quick datapoint: node gpu-uw2-03 reported provider preempt SIG and then nv_peer_mem ECC errors. Pods were evicted by our node-watcher within ~12s. Affected tenant has pinned model variant rdl-13b-v1 (FP16) on that node. Other nodes show normal KV cache hit rates.

eng-runtime-sam: FYI I've seen pattern like this with spot preempts + long KV flush holding up eviction. Will look at fallback routing and KV persistence. Can we divert traffic off pool immediately?

oncall-jordan: Actions: 1) cordon node, 2) drain remaining tenant pods, 3) failover tenant to fallback pool (reserved-burst-1), 4) scale-up reserved-burst if needed. Running commands now.

ops-kyra: running drain command:
```
rictl node cordon gpu-uw2-03 --reason "preempt_signal"
rictl node drain gpu-uw2-03 --grace-period 10 --force-evict --evict-list tenant:CeruleanHealth
```

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline paused for pools referencing gpu-uw2-03. Build #4821 suspended.

se-helena: Notifying Cerulean Health SRE (pager) per escalation plan. Sending brief with ETA ~10-20m for migration. Will mention potential 5–10% degraded throughput while we warm fallback cache.

infra-miguel: Provider events: marked as spot-interruptible (preempt window 30s). Policy shows automatic replacement requested. Opening node replacement ticket with cloud provider.

eng-runtime-sam: Starting route change: update routing policy for tenant CeruleanHealth => prefer reserved-burst-1, fall back to rdl-13b-v1-quant if latency spikes. Patch applied, verifying.

ops-kyra: Observability: 503 spike started at 1988123448 and peaked at +18% error rate. After drain started, errors tapered. Logs:
```
[1988123450] nv_peer_mem: ECC 0x1f at addr 0x7fff...
[1988123451] kworker/3: kernel oops: GPU watchdog timeout
```

oncall-jordan: Handing off to ops-kyra for mitigation and to eng-runtime-sam for routing verification. I need to step off for another page — @ops-kyra take lead, please confirm when tenant is steady and then coordinate customer update.

ops-kyra: I have lead. Current status:
- Node cordoned+drained: yes
- Tenant moved to reserved-burst-1: yes (traffic shifted ~100% at 1988123482)
- KV cache warmups: in progress, expected steady state in ~4–6 min
- Errors back to baseline (503s < 1.5%) as of 1988123495 :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-sam: Routing check: all requests now hitting reserved-burst-1 and hitting quantized fallback when model loading takes >500ms. Added temporary throttle to client concurrency for CeruleanHealth to avoid cold-start thundering herd.

se-helena: Sent update to Cerulean Health: short note that we detected preemption, migrated workload to reserved capacity, recovering. Offered follow-up postmortem. They acknowledged and asked for impact window.

ops-kyra: Impact window estimate: 1988123448 - 1988123495. Max error rate +18% for ~47s. Will include logs and remediation steps in incident summary.

infra-miguel: Replacement node request confirmed with provider; replacement node provisioning started at 1988123502. ETA ~12m to join pool.

deploy-bot: Noted. Resuming pipelines that were paused once the pool is back to expected capacity.

eng-runtime-sam: Quick note — we pushed a temporary rollout to prefer quantized model for CeruleanHealth to reduce memory pressure on the replacement node. Will revert after capacity normalizes.

ops-kyra: Monitoring: CPU/GPU temps stable on remaining nodes. No additional ECC counts seen. I'll keep a 30m watch. Scheduling immediate postmortem with infra and runtime for 0900 UTC tomorrow.

oncall-jordan: Thanks team. I confirmed handoff in PagerDuty. Closing my oncall rotation for this page. @ops-kyra you're primary; @eng-runtime-sam secondary.

ops-kyra: Final update: replacement node joined at 1988123568, node-health checks passed. Migrated tenant back to vault-prod-ded-2 by 1988123679 during low-traffic window. Reverted temporary quantized preference at 1988123690. All metrics normal; closing incident thread. Will attach runbook steps + logs to postmortem.

se-helena: Customer notified with final impact summary and remediation timeline. They asked for confirmation that their dedicated pool will be excluded from spot-backed hosts — I've started an enterprise support ticket to review dedicated pool affinity settings.

eng-runtime-sam: Action items for postmortem:
- verify KV flush behaviour during drain and tighten eviction timeout
- add graceful migration hook to preempt path to reduce cold-starts
- validate dedicated pool placement policies for enterprise pools

ops-kyra: Filing PIR. Linking logs: <obf_link>/logs/1988123456 and alert graph. Tagging incident severity P1 -> postmortem required.

incident-bot: Incident closed by ops-kyra at 1988123898. Postmortem scheduled.

infra-miguel: thumbs-up and will follow up on provider placement settings.

oncall-jordan: Closing thread. Good job everyone. :partyparrot:
